Course: SOC101
Faculty: MSRz
It's his first semester at NSU, and if you love sociology, then he's the best for you.
Syllabus: The syllabus is extensive, including 14 chapters, 7 for mid-terms and 7 for finals, whereas other faculty's syllabus is much shorter.
Quizzes: He took three quizzes, of which the best two are considered. The quizzes consisted of MCQs, and they were directly from the slides.
Mid-term and Final: The mid-term and final exams consisted of short and broad questions, and he provided suggestions that were more than enough, and everything came from his suggestions. Reading the book is a must for mid and final as he wants elaborate answers, and it's better to avoid bullet points while answering the questions. (Pro-tip: Use examples cz he loves examples)
Assignments: There's a group research proposal, and instead of a presentation, he took an individual reflective essay.
Grading: In terms of grading, he is very strict and doesn't curve a bit. Also, he deducts marks for being absent without proper reason.
If you stay focused and understand the topic properly, you are good to go.

izs.review:
SOC101 – IZS
I was in my very first semester and got IZS ma'am as my faculty. I was absolutely terrified after seeing the reviews. But at the end of the semester, I realized it isn't that difficult to get a good grade from her. Yes, she is not easygoing; she doesn't curve at all, and there are tons of assessments in her course as well, but if you stay consistent throughout the semester, it is possible to score nearly full marks on every assessment.
These are the techniques I personally followed that helped me get a good grade:
1. Start interacting with ma'am from the very first class, and it is a must as she herself expects students to engage in classroom discussions. It still won't make her biased toward you though 
2. Never ever miss any homework, as she checks each and every line of your writing.
3. Watch the movies/documentaries and read the articles on time. Try to connect them with sociological concepts, as exam questions often require relating particular scenes to concepts discussed in class.
4. Take notes in class, especially the specific examples, as they help a lot in exams.
5. Don't read the whole book. Focus on the specific parts she tells you to read.
6. Solve the questions at the end of the lecture slides before the exams.
7. Write concisely in exams. She gives full marks even if you can explain concepts properly in just 4–5 lines.
8. You can easily lose marks in the debate, so don’t hesitate to ask your debater friends for help.
9. For the oral presentation, choose the topics you have the strongest grasp of. Memorize everything given in the slides and add relevant examples as well.
10. Form a good group for the research paper. Good groupmates make the experience much smoother.
11. For the paper presentation, just maintain proper eye contact and try to deliver your speech fluently.
Best of luck!

thanks for pointing these things out. getting a good grade under IZS is tough but i believe if you work hard and play your moves smartly, you can manage to get through with flying colors. might be a little too much effort for a SOC course but better than having to pay another 20K for it again.
